subject: Post-call recap: Acme Health private VPC / on‑prem requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Foster <daniel.foster@acmehealth.com>, Priyanka Shah <priyanka.shah@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Acme Health private VPC / on‑prem requirements

Hi Daniel & Priyanka —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to keep momentum: we captured the key constraints and goals below. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of pain & drivers
- Regulatory: PHI in-scope for several AI-assisted workflows (HIPAA). Customer requirement: no PHI leaves Acme network for those workloads.
- Data residency: Primary processing must remain in US regions; some teams require on‑prem/air‑gapped option for controlled research environments.
- Networking constraints: Strict egress controls, outbound internet blocked for certain subnet(s); customers require either a private VPC deployment or on‑prem (air‑gapped) package with an isolated control plane.
- Security evidence: Acme will need SOC 2 summary, pen test results, and KMS/HSM integration options for key management.

Goals (what success looks like)
1) Proof-of-concept: private VPC deployment in Acme's AWS account (no public internet egress for PHI workloads).
2) Architecture that supports both hosted control plane (with private connectivity) and an air-gapped on‑prem option for sensitive workloads.
3) Clear mutual action plan and procurement timeline (3–4 month target to POC, then production pilot).

Immediate next steps
- I’ll share a short architecture diagram and SOC2 summary (attached). ACTION: Marissa to send Redwood private VPC reference architecture and SOC2 summary — sent.
- Technical workshop: schedule a session with Mateo (solutions engineer) to walk networking/security requirements and confirm feasible connectivity patterns (VPC endpoints, Transit Gateway, or private link options). ACTION: Acme to share network diagram and list of security controls that must be enforced.
- Procurement/contract: we’ll share a draft mutual action plan and initial SOW for review.

Attachments included: redwood-private-vpc-arch.pdf, SOC2-summary.pdf. I’ve also uploaded the mutual-action-plan.xlsx to the Drive link below.

Proposed dates for the technical workshop: Thu 23 Jul or Mon 27 Jul — please let us know which works best.

Thanks — looking forward to the workshop.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Acme Health private VPC / on‑prem requirements

Thanks Marissa — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Correct, any workload processing PHI must not egress to public internet or third‑party hosted control planes unless it's within an approved private connection.
- For research teams, we will likely require an air‑gapped on‑prem option for a subset of models; that can be a later phase but needs to be in scope.
- Timeline: procurement expects a POC kickoff in early October; however the security review can start sooner if we have the architecture + SOC2 summary.

I’ll coordinate with Priyanka and the IT security group to get a network diagram and a list of required controls (firewall rules, approved TLS profiles, IP allowlists, and any mandatory HSM vendors).

On scheduling the workshop, Thu 23 Jul is tight for us — Mon 27 Jul looks better. Can Mateo and Camila do the 27th morning PST?

Thanks,
Daniel
Director, Data Platforms | Acme Health
